analysis: Only scripts/test-provider-release-toolchain.py changed: an added `import shutil` (head line 5) and a new ReleaseCMakeTests class (head lines 66-117). It is a unit test that stubs uname and curl in a temp dir, builds a fake RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE, and runs scripts/install-release-cmake.sh. It asserts that a complete, exact-version tool-cache CMake is used without a download, and that an absent, incomplete or other-version cache triggers a download attempt (curl exit 7 propagates, nothing is written to GITHUB_PATH). No production code, coordinator/provider protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization or cache-storage behavior changes, so none of the canonical threat model's assets or boundaries (e.g. T-041, the only supplied definition) are touched. The tests use only temp directories and stubbed binaries, with no real network access or secrets. Security-relevant behavior lives in the unseen install-release-cmake.sh, which is not in this batch. Whether that script verifies a checksum or signature on the downloaded CMake tarball, and whether trusting the runner-image tool-cache copy is acceptable, cannot be judged from this test file. The test only asserts that the download URL is for v3.31.12 and that PATH is untouched on failure. Any toolchain supply-chain concern belongs to a review of the script itself and is not a finding here. No regression identified in the supplied units.
